project.name: scout-ui
project.productType: open-source React design library and documentation product

typography.display: Bricolage Grotesque target with robust local system fallback
typography.body: Inter target with robust local system fallback
typography.code: Geist Mono target with robust local system fallback

radius.language: bounded shape vocabulary; labels, paper, stamps, and true pills remain distinct

shadows.language: hard offset shadows communicate physical depth and state

motion.language: bounded, local, optional, and reduced-motion safe

design.density: calm technical reading with expressive local interruptions

must: Preserve native semantics and visible focus
Keep structure predictable while expression stays bounded
Use paper and night as compositional surfaces
Respect reduced motion, forced colors, touch, and reflow
avoid: Generic SaaS dashboards and uniform card grids
Glassmorphism, soft gradients, and excessive rounded pills
External runtime fonts or unlicensed assets
M13 controls, schemas, presets, or URL state during M12

decisions: M12 uses calm paper reading regions and bounded night preview regions on the same page.
The component index uses authored pinboard hierarchy without changing semantic order.
Root layout and route content remain server components; browser state lives in small client leaves.
The documentation shell dogfoods StickerNavbar and the frozen Scout UI packages.
No 21st AI generation was used; the authoritative Scout UI specifications define the visual direction.
M13 uses one typed component registry to drive the full playground and compact component-page control rail, with a 7/5 desktop workbench and one Radix bottom sheet on mobile.
M13 control actions remain in normal document flow so Reset, Share, status, and fallback content never cover schema fields.
M13 keeps the preview as a bounded night board and the controls as a paper control sheet; component expression changes inside that stable workbench rather than redesigning the shell per route.
